rounds.proof_sketch: The epsilon change from 1e-5 to 1.01e-5 causes inv_std to change by factor sqrt(1.01)≈1.00499, yielding ~0.495% relative error. Since rtol=1% always exceeds this, |error|=0.00495×|ref| < 0.01+0.01×|ref|=threshold for all ref values.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation introduces a 1% increase in epsilon, which affects the inverse standard deviation computation. When variance approaches zero, the maximum relative change in inv_std is sqrt(1.01e-5/1e-5)-1 ≈ 0.495%. This relative error is strictly less than the rtol=1% tolerance. For any output magnitude, the error scales as ~0.5% of the output, while the tolerance scales as 1% of the output plus 0.01 absolute. The tolerance always exceeds the error, making this mutant mathematically equivalent under the given tolerances.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable: The ~0.5% maximum relative error from the epsilon perturbation is strictly below the 1% relative tolerance. No input values can cause the error to exceed atol + rtol × |ref|.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing epsilon parameters, use tighter tolerances (e.g., rtol=1e-3) to detect small numerical perturbations. The current 1% tolerance masks any epsilon change smaller than ~4%.
